---
title: Block Format
---

A block keeps the instruction in plain text and attaches a detached signature after it, in the
manner of an OpenPGP cleartext signature. Nothing in the block is encoded except the signature
segment, so the text a reader sees is the text the signature covers.


## Envelope

A block is a sequence of lines:

```
-----BEGIN SIB SIGNED INSTRUCTION-----
<instruction: one or more lines>
-----BEGIN SIB SIGNATURE-----
<clear metadata lines: zero or more "Name: value" lines>
<one blank line, present when there are metadata lines>
<signature segment: base64url text, wrapped>
-----END SIB SIGNATURE-----
```

Marker lines
: Each marker is three or more dashes, the marker name, then three or more dashes. A signer MUST
  emit exactly five ASCII hyphen-minus characters (U+002D) on each side. A verifier MUST accept
  any run of three or more characters from the set U+002D, U+2010 to U+2015 and U+2212 on either
  side, since editors and chat clients substitute dashes silently.

Transport prefix
: A verifier MUST strip from every line of the block the prefix that precedes the dashes on the
  opening marker line (for instance `> `, `# ` or `// `), when the line starts with that prefix.
  A line consisting only of that prefix, with or without trailing whitespace, is a blank line.

Instruction segment
: Every line between the first and second markers, joined with U+000A, with leading and trailing
  blank lines removed. The signature covers this text after canonicalization, not the bytes as
  written.

Clear metadata lines
: Lines of the form `Name: value` at the top of the signature block, ended by the first blank
  line. A signer MUST emit `Signer`, `Expires` and, when the header has `aud`, `Audience`, with
  the same values as the header fields `iss`, `exp` and `aud`. They are conveniences for readers.
  A verifier MUST compare each one it recognizes with the signed header and MUST report
  `metadata_mismatch` when they differ. Unknown names are ignored.

Signature segment
: The JWS compact serialization `BASE64URL(header) . . BASE64URL(signature)`: three segments
  separated by two dots with an empty middle segment, because the payload is detached. A signer
  MUST wrap it at 64 columns. A verifier MUST discard every character of the segment that is not
  in the base64url alphabet (`A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `-`, `_`) or a dot before parsing it,
  which makes re-wrapping and quoting harmless.

A document MAY contain any number of blocks. A verifier MUST process each independently. A block
whose closing marker is missing MUST be skipped, never repaired.


## Header

The first segment is the base64url encoding of the header serialized with RFC 8785. The header is
signed. Field names follow JOSE and JWT where a registered name exists.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alg` | string | yes | Signature algorithm from the closed list below. |
| `typ` | string | yes | Specification version. MUST be `SIB/1`. |
| `kid` | string | yes | Key identifier, looked up in the signer registry. Conventionally `<signer>#<label>`. |
| `b64` | boolean | yes | MUST be `false`: the instruction is an unencoded, detached payload (RFC 7797). |
| `crit` | array of string | yes | MUST contain `b64`. Other entries name extensions the verifier must understand. |
| `canon` | string | yes | Canonicalization rule applied to the instruction, from the [registry](canonicalization.qmd#rule-registry). |
| `iss` | string | yes | Issuer: the signer's stable identifier. |
| `iat` | string | yes | Issued at, RFC 3339 UTC with `Z`, whole seconds. |
| `exp` | string | yes | Expires at, same format. MUST be later than `iat`. |
| `jti` | string | yes | Unique identifier for this block; the replay nonce. At least 96 bits of randomness, base64url. |
| `aud` | string | no | Audience: the deployment or harness that may honor the block. Required in enforced mode. |
| `mode` | string | yes | `dev` for a software key, `enforced` for a hardware-backed key. |
| `credentialId` | string | `ES256-webauthn` only | The WebAuthn credential id, base64url. MUST equal the credential enrolled under `kid`. |
| `authenticatorData` | string | `ES256-webauthn` only | The assertion's authenticator data, base64url. |
| `clientDataJSON` | string | `ES256-webauthn` only | The assertion's client data, base64url of the exact bytes the authenticator signed over. |

A signer MUST NOT list `canon` in `crit`: a generic JWS library must be able to accept the header,
and canonicalization is applied by the signer and the verifier before the bytes reach the
signature primitive. The three assertion fields MUST be present, and non-empty, when `alg` is
`ES256-webauthn` and MUST be absent otherwise.

### Algorithms

| `alg` | Status | Signature primitive |
|---|---|---|
| `EdDSA` | normative | Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over the signing input. |
| `ES256-webauthn` | normative | ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over `authenticatorData ‖ SHA-256(clientDataJSON)`, in the ASN.1 DER form the authenticator returns, with the WebAuthn challenge equal to `BASE64URL(SHA-256(signing input))` computed over the header without the three assertion fields. The verifier MUST require the user-verification flag. See [WebAuthn Assertion](#webauthn-assertion). |

A verifier MUST reject any other value with status `malformed`.


## Signing Input

The signing input is the RFC 7797 form:

```
ASCII(BASE64URL(UTF8(header JSON))) ‖ "." ‖ UTF8(canonical instruction)
```

The canonical instruction is the instruction segment after the rule named in `canon`. For `EdDSA`
the signature is computed over the signing input with the primitive named in `alg`. For
`ES256-webauthn` the signing input is hashed into the WebAuthn challenge, as the next section
describes, and the header JSON in it is the signing header: the block's header with
`credentialId`, `authenticatorData` and `clientDataJSON` removed.


## WebAuthn Assertion

A WebAuthn authenticator signs a challenge, not a document. The `ES256-webauthn` path binds the
block to the challenge:

1. The signer builds the signing header (every field except the three assertion fields),
   computes the signing input over it and the canonical instruction, and sets

   ```
   challenge = SHA-256(signing input)
   ```

2. The authenticator performs a `webauthn.get` ceremony with that challenge, user verification
   required, on the origin and RP ID enrolled for the key. It returns `authenticatorData`,
   `clientDataJSON` and a signature over `authenticatorData ‖ SHA-256(clientDataJSON)`.
   `clientDataJSON` carries `BASE64URL(challenge)` as the authenticator saw it.

3. The signer adds `credentialId`, `authenticatorData` and `clientDataJSON` to the header,
   base64url, and emits the block with the authenticator's signature as the third segment.

A verifier recomputes the challenge from the block's header (minus the assertion fields) and the
canonical instruction, and compares it with the one inside `clientDataJSON`. A change to the
instruction or to any signed header field changes the recomputed challenge, so the block fails with
`invalid_signature` even though the authenticator's signature over `clientDataJSON` still holds.
The full check sequence is in [Verification](verification.qmd#algorithm).

The header JSON is serialized with RFC 8785 rules (sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8), so removing
three fields and re-encoding reproduces the signing header byte for byte.


## Example (Dev Mode)

Produced with the reference implementation in dev mode. It verifies against the registry entry
below with audience `acme/dev-agent` at any time before the `Expires` value.

```
-----BEGIN SIB SIGNED INSTRUCTION-----
You may deploy the current main branch to staging with
scripts/deploy.sh staging whenever the test suite passes.
-----BEGIN SIB SIGNATURE-----
Signer: alice@example.com
Expires: 2026-09-13T22:07:11Z
Audience: acme/dev-agent

eyJhbGciOiJFZERTQSIsImF1ZCI6ImFjbWUvZGV2LWFnZW50IiwiYjY0IjpmYWxz
ZSwiY2Fub24iOiJ0ZXh0LzEiLCJjcml0IjpbImI2NCJdLCJleHAiOiIyMDI2LTA5
LTEzVDIyOjA3OjExWiIsImlhdCI6IjIwMjYtMDktMTNUMTQ6MDc6MTFaIiwiaXNz
IjoiYWxpY2VAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20iLCJqdGkiOiJFUEM3dk5fSDBWcV80RXVIIiwi
a2lkIjoiYWxpY2VAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20jZGV2LTIwMjYtMDkiLCJtb2RlIjoiZGV2
IiwidHlwIjoiU0lCLzEifQ..7AR5HWCArFFXd9L46wA3_70TpECOXflcTkHa_Fac
dY7eIHc4Sk9X6T7D9gR4rE6j17tdC9isvrMId_gNDnW5Dw
-----END SIB SIGNATURE-----
```

The decoded header:

```json
{
  "alg": "EdDSA",
  "typ": "SIB/1",
  "kid": "alice@example.com#dev-2026-09",
  "b64": false,
  "crit": ["b64"],
  "canon": "text/1",
  "iss": "alice@example.com",
  "iat": "2026-09-13T14:07:11Z",
  "exp": "2026-09-13T22:07:11Z",
  "jti": "EPC7vN_H0Vq_4EuH",
  "aud": "acme/dev-agent",
  "mode": "dev"
}
```

The canonical instruction under `text/1`, which is the payload of the signing input:

```
You may deploy the current main branch to staging with scripts/deploy.sh staging whenever the test suite passes.
```

The registry entry the verifier uses:

```json
{
  "signer": "alice@example.com",
  "keys": [
    {
      "kid": "alice@example.com#dev-2026-09",
      "alg": "EdDSA",
      "public_key": "o3T5RIEeC0AJG78bmD4WAOWpNxAXgMDAbQV0vCfAxyQ",
      "mode": "dev",
      "enrolled_at": "2026-09-13T14:07:11Z",
      "attestation_verified": false,
      "revoked": false
    }
  ]
}
```

`public_key` is the 32-byte Ed25519 public key, base64url without padding.


## Example (Passkey)

Produced by `sib sign` through the sign page in Chromium with a virtual authenticator (CTAP2,
internal transport, user verification on). The same instruction, signed in enforced mode:

The decoded header:

```json
{
  "alg": "ES256-webauthn",
  "typ": "SIB/1",
  "kid": "alice@example.com#passkey-9188",
  "b64": false,
  "crit": ["b64"],
  "canon": "text/1",
  "iss": "alice@example.com",
  "iat": "2026-10-05T11:45:21Z",
  "exp": "2026-10-05T19:45:21Z",
  "jti": "MnLlnQorJ1qvA13H",
  "aud": "acme/dev-agent",
  "mode": "enforced",
  "credentialId": "kYjC6VVDjNGdsK9jHcPPariB-AUWC8KDxWLVH-Vp9p4",
  "authenticatorData": "SZYN5YgOjGh0NBcPZHZgW4_krrmihjLHmVzzuoMdl2MFAAAAAw",
  "clientDataJSON": "eyJ0eXBlIjoid2ViYXV0aG4uZ2V0IiwiY2hhbGxlbmdlIjoidjdtaVk5cHJ5UnJmRGpwVDVRSUNJR2xEbUpoVzRqRkkxakhuTXVaSk9zUSIsIm9yaWdpbiI6Imh0dHA6Ly9sb2NhbGhvc3Q6NzM5MSIsImNyb3NzT3JpZ2luIjpmYWxzZX0"
}
```

`clientDataJSON` decodes to the bytes the authenticator signed over; its `challenge` is the
SHA-256 of the signing input over the header without the three assertion fields:

```json
{"type":"webauthn.get","challenge":"v7miY9pryRrfDjpT5QICIGlDmJhW4jFI1jHnMuZJOsQ","origin":"http://localhost:7391","crossOrigin":false}
```

`authenticatorData` is 37 bytes: the SHA-256 of the RP ID `localhost` (`49960de5880e8c68…`), the
flags byte `0x05` (UP and UV set) and the signature counter `3`. The signature segment is the
authenticator's DER-encoded ECDSA signature. The registry entry the verifier uses:

```json
{
  "signer": "alice@example.com",
  "keys": [
    {
      "kid": "alice@example.com#passkey-9188",
      "alg": "ES256-webauthn",
      "public_key": "pQECAyYgASFYIAme6lzACHBimeQ_-XoqnWCJGkWnolTu63bWExx4t1mZIlggf_dOOJAncBQ8B9jE1koWCovF_qJejGQv_fBEm2QL1oY",
      "mode": "enforced",
      "enrolled_at": "2026-10-05T11:45:20Z",
      "attestation_verified": false,
      "attestation": {"format": "packed", "x5c_present": true, "roots": null},
      "revoked": false,
      "credential_id": "kYjC6VVDjNGdsK9jHcPPariB-AUWC8KDxWLVH-Vp9p4",
      "aaguid": "01020304-0506-0708-0102-030405060708",
      "sign_count": 1,
      "origins": ["http://localhost:7391"],
      "rp_id": "localhost",
      "transports": ["internal"]
    }
  ]
}
```

`public_key` is the COSE-encoded P-256 public key, base64url without padding. The virtual
authenticator's AAGUID is not on the built-in allowlist, so this block verifies only against a
registry that adds it under `allowed_aaguids`, which is the configuration the example was produced
with.
